claim_summary: For a prescribed perimeter and outward normals constrained to an equally spaced planar grid, odd grid orders have an explicit sharp positive minimum area uniquely attained by an isosceles-triangle rotation orbit; even orders have infimum zero. The regular grid polygon has the maximal area, and the full intermediate area interval is attained.
integrity: All deductions described in the result use standard planar Minkowski existence, Brunn--Minkowski concavity, a finite-dimensional vertex argument, strict cotangent convexity, and the established polygonal upper isoperimetric inequality. No independent verification or priority certification is claimed.
scientific_limitations: Planar evenly spaced finite outward-normal grids only; no general arbitrary normal set theorem.
The minimum for odd orders above three is approached but not attained if every grid direction is required to carry positive edge length.
Full text of one relevant 2026 source was not wholly accessible; unindexed prior results remain a priority risk.
The standalone finite checks corroborate, not replace, the universal analytic proof.
title: Sharp reverse isoperimetry on circular normal grids
